column1: # Norwegian Bokmal (nb) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); Norwegian has the same
#                                 one (1) | other rule, so the translation lists two forms
#            @msg                 a status or error message; templated ones keep `{name}`
#            @msgplural           a plural status or error message, one|other
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry is written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Norwegian Bokmal vector-drawing vocabulary (ankepunkt, bane, strek, fyll, monteringsflate,
# banebehandler ...). No proprietary localisation resource, string table or product UI was
# consulted or copied; add entries the same way. Product and technology names (VectorCraft,
# ArtCraft, SVG, OpenType, CMYK, Lab ...) stay in Latin letters; the trailing "..." of dialog
# commands is kept. Terms shared with PhotoCraft use the same words as its nb catalog
# (lag, utvalg, innstillinger, blandingsmodus ...), so the two apps read alike.
# AI-assisted; independent native proofreading remains follow-up work.
